summary: Eight comment-endorsed discoveries spanning filtered news, civic data, computer simulation, energy analysis, and books.
telegram_footer: 8 items surfaced | 30/30 past front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated

items.name: unslop.news
items.source_story_title: Software occlusion culling in Block Game
items.summary: A filtered Hacker News front page that removes AI-related submissions.
items.why_included: A concrete news-reading alternative explicitly endorsed in a technical thread.
items.evidence: A commenter calls unslop.news a good tool in a discussion about finding technical articles on HN.

items.name: Civic Mined
items.summary: A civic-data search service covering municipal records, budgets, meetings, and permits.
items.why_included: Its creator reports useful personal interactions with local government, beyond merely announcing a project.
items.evidence: The creator says Civic Mined exposes municipal documents and data through MCP and has been very helpful in personal dealings with local government; this is creator-reported use, not independent validation.

evidence_sources.author: janj
evidence_sources.excerpt: I've used it a number of times for personal interactions with my local government, it's been very helpful.

items.name: NAND-16
items.source_story_title: NAND-16: a computer built from 277,248 NAND gates
items.summary: An interactive 16-bit computer simulation built from NAND gates; praised for its visuals.
items.why_included: A comment independently praises the interactive result rather than merely naming the submission.
items.evidence: A commenter calls NAND-16 well done, interactive, and visually strong, regardless of AI involvement.

evidence_sources.author: tails4e
evidence_sources.excerpt: I think this is very cool. AI generated or not, its well done, interactive and has great visuals.

items.name: Has It Held Up? — Without the Hot Air
items.source_story_title: Sustainable energy without the hot air (2008)
items.summary: An energy-book retrospective checking David MacKay's assumptions against subsequent developments.
items.why_included: A directly recommended entry point separates the book's enduring method from outdated numbers.
items.evidence: A commenter recommends the Has It Held Up? section as a very good entry point.

evidence_sources.author: laurencerowe
evidence_sources.excerpt: The 'Has It Held Up?' section seems a very good entry point.

items.name: Understanding Comics
items.source_story_title: Ask HN: What are you reading?
items.summary: Scott McCloud's comic-book guide to visual storytelling; readers describe perspective-changing insights.
items.why_included: Two readers give specific, first-hand praise for how the book changes reading comics.
items.evidence: One reader reports many aha moments and recommends the book to comics readers or creators; a lifelong comics fan says it changed how they read comics.

evidence_sources.author: mysterydip
evidence_sources.excerpt: I just finished Scott McCloud’s Understanding Comics and it had so many “aha” moments for me. Definitely recommended if you have even a passing interest in reading or making graphic novels or comics.

evidence_sources.author: dam_jackalopes
evidence_sources.excerpt: So, so good. Changed the way I read comics and I've been a lifelong fan of the medium.

items.name: Countdown to Zero Day
items.source_story_title: Ask HN: What are you reading?
items.summary: Kim Zetter's detailed history of Stuxnet; recommended despite its length.
items.why_included: The recommendation identifies concrete depth on a consequential malware operation.
items.evidence: A commenter recommends the in-depth Stuxnet history while noting that it is a bit long and does not include code.

evidence_sources.author: jadijadi
evidence_sources.excerpt: An indepth history of Stuxnet. A bit long but recommended. You can not find any other book which goes this much in describing a mallware (no code).

items.name: Ra by qntm
items.source_story_title: Ask HN: What are you reading?
items.summary: A freely readable science-fantasy novel where magic becomes an engineering discipline.
items.why_included: An explicit recommendation from a reader who finished it supports a free direct reading link.
items.evidence: A reader who finished Ra says they greatly enjoyed it and strongly recommend it, noting that it is free on the author's website.

evidence_sources.author: 1potato
evidence_sources.excerpt: If you haven't read Ra, though, I greatly enjoyed it and would strongly recommend it.

items.name: Agatha Christie — Standard Ebooks collection
items.source_story_title: Ask HN: What are you reading?
items.summary: Carefully produced Agatha Christie ebooks for readers wanting classic mysteries.
items.why_included: A specific author collection is endorsed as an accessible mystery-reading starting point.
items.evidence: A reader praises Christie's writing and calls the Standard Ebooks editions an easy pick for readers interested in mysteries.
